routes.title: Routes to a limbless or limb-reduced mouse
routes.note: Published perturbations and bounded proposals, grouped by the scale they act at. Every row carries its own evidence level and read levels on its sources. None has been attempted here.

studies.title: The ZRS across species: what changes when a limb enhancer is swapped
studies.question: Kvon et al. replaced the mouse ZRS with orthologs and got normal limbs from some species and truncated limbs from others. What, in the sequence itself, separates the two groups?
studies.summary: Real ZRS orthologs fetched from NCBI, aligned here, with per-column conservation and ETS-motif positions. The contrast of interest is between the orthologs that gave normal limbs in the published knock-in and the one that truncated them. This is a correlational reading of a handful of sequences; it is not a predictor of enhancer activity and is not used as one anywhere on this page.

figures.alt: Per-column conservation of aligned ZRS orthologs with ETS motif positions marked, species coloured by the limb phenotype their knock-in produced
figures.caption: Sequence analysis. Per-column conservation across the ZRS orthologs retrieved, with ETS motif positions marked.

studies.title: The SHH–GREM1–FGF loop: where a weakened enhancer stops being a weaker limb and starts being no limb
studies.question: The limb bud is held open by a feedback loop. If a ZRS allele lowers ZPA Shh output, is the result proportionally smaller, or is there a threshold below which the loop never engages at all?
studies.summary: An ODE model of the SHH–GREM1–BMP–FGF feedback loop, built from the published topology with every rate constant marked sourced or assumed. The wild-type control must initiate, sustain and self-terminate before any sweep is read. Three knobs are then swept — ZPA Shh output, AER-inducing FGF10 input, and GREM1 production — because three different routes on this page act on three different parts of the same loop.

figures.alt: Simulated time courses of SHH, GREM1, BMP and FGF under wild-type parameters, showing the loop engaging and then self-terminating
figures.caption: Simulation, control arm. Wild-type parameters: the loop engages, is sustained for a bounded window, and self-terminates.

figures.alt: Simulated outgrowth duration against the fraction of wild-type ZPA Shh output, showing a sharp threshold
figures.caption: Simulation. Outgrowth duration against the fraction of wild-type ZPA Shh output. The threshold is a property of this model, not a measurement in an embryo.

figures.alt: Simulated two-dimensional phase map over Shh output and FGF10 input, coloured by phenotype class
figures.caption: Simulation. Two knobs at once: the same phenotype class is reachable from different directions, which is the point of a design space.

studies.title: Skeletal elements as a Turing pattern: how small a limb bud can be and still make a digit
studies.question: If a truncated bud is a smaller field, how small does the field have to get before it patterns no complete skeletal element at all?
studies.summary: A two-dimensional BMP–SOX9–WNT reaction–diffusion model on a limb-bud-shaped domain, with its own linear-stability analysis as an internal control. Element counts come from a pre-declared objective criterion, not from looking at the pictures, and the spread across random seeds is reported because Turing patterns are seed-dependent.

figures.alt: Simulated digit-like pattern in a limb-bud-shaped domain
figures.caption: Simulation. The pattern the model makes in a full-size paddle.

figures.alt: A strip of simulated patterns across the parameter sweep, from several elements down to none, each labelled with its element count
figures.caption: Simulation. The same model across the sweep, from several elements down to none.

figures.alt: Simulated element count against domain size, with the critical domain size marked
figures.caption: Simulation. Element count against domain size, in units of the pattern's own wavelength.
